claims: Artemis II is a ~10-day mission.
Artemis II sends four astronauts around the Moon.
Artemis II uses a figure-eight free-return trajectory.
Artemis II is launched by the SLS rocket from Kennedy Space Center.
Orion spacecraft performs two Earth orbits for system checks.
Orion spacecraft executes a Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn.
Crew loops around the far side of the Moon up to 6,513 km from the surface.
Mission returns to a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
Rocket launches from Florida into a high-elliptical Earth orbit.
Rocket performs two laps to test systems.
On the second orbit, the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) fires to increase speed.
ICPS firing sends the crew toward the Moon.
Outbound transit is a four-day journey towards the Moon.
Crew tests the Orion spacecraft's manual handling.
Crew tests the Orion spacecraft's radiation shielding.
Orion passes 6,479–6,519 km above the Moon's far side.
Lunar flyby uses the Moon's gravity to slingshot the spacecraft back toward Earth.
Lunar flyby does not enter a long-term orbit.
Return transit is a four-day return trip.
Service module separates 75 miles above Earth.
Crew module reenters the atmosphere at ~25,000 mph.
Reentry is shielded from temperatures near 5,000°F.
Mission is designed to go farther from Earth than the Apollo 13 record.
Mission traverses the far side of the Moon for the first time in over 50 years
